judgements.justification: A's AC rejected against a 3-to-1 positive panel with no score moved, on its own verdict that 'the technical contributions and the writing quality do not meet the bar', below what A's scores supported.
Neither committee rested its recommendation on a forecast of broad impact.
B's Reviewer_1j5f moved toward acceptance after the rebuttal met its main concern (non-local baseline); no A score moved.
Each committee had one light review (A: 1xyW, B: hB4H); neither committee's reviews as a whole had less scrutiny than the other's.
Only A's rPEM judged the Something-Something margins small and the rebuttal's Kinetics baselines weak, and A's AC adopted that list in the reject.
Both committees named unclear writing, incrementality and missing Kinetics; B's reviewers called them addressed and rated 7/6/7, while A's AC called them disqualifying.
No score moved in A after the discussion; iQAh and KG6i echoed rPEM's writing point but kept 6 and 7.
rPEM's 5 rests on the weaknesses in its limitations box, so its rating is not clearly out of line with its own text.
All reviewers had confidence 3 or 4 and none said they could not judge the paper.
A's AC restated the lone detractor rPEM's late comment nearly verbatim, down to 'kind of incremental', and set aside three positive scores.
The reviewers' scores nearly match across committees; the split came from the ACs, not from a calibration gap fed through the mean.
B's AC gave a spotlight on 'unanimously positive rates' with no rating above 7, while A's 5 held it lower at the same maximum.
B's score rise rested on new experiments the authors ran themselves; the copy error in one row did not change the conclusion.
B's three-sentence meta-review names no weakness, not even L4t3's 'a bit incremental and convoluted', while A's meta-review carried its reviewers' reservations forward.
The wrong claims (1xyW's CUDA, hB4H's Eq. 5, iQAh's Table 2) did not feed either committee's scores or recommendation.
The authors' concessions (Kinetics setting below SOTA, simplified Eq. 3) went to both committees and do not concern results that a stronger baseline beat.

rPEM posted 'not that significant' and 'kind of incremental' on 2021-08-29, after the rebuttal, with no author reply in the record, and A's AC adopted them; B's objections came before the rebuttal and were answered.
A's AC applied its own reading and rPEM's list, not a different cut-off on near-identical scores.
Neither AC passed over a clearly best-informed reviewer; B's most careful reviewer L4t3 rated 7 and B accepted.
B's main concerns (non-local baseline, parameter counts) were closable by new results, and 1j5f rose; A's decisive concerns (writing, incrementality) no rebuttal table could fix.
rPEM's 5 did not set the tier through the mean; A's AC rejected on its adopted framing against a 6.0 mean.
rPEM replied to the rebuttal and posted in the discussion.
A's AC did not discard its detractor; it followed it.
No reviewer or AC raised audience breadth or venue fit.
Neither meta-review misreported the reviewers' final positions or the rebuttal.
All reviewers in both committees replied to the rebuttal.
No reviewer said they could not verify the main results.
A's panel split 3-to-1, not evenly.
The rebuttal row '32.0 G, 23.3 M, 43.2' is labelled Involution to A and NL w/ R.P.E to B, so the committees saw conflicting numbers, although the conclusion holds either way.
rPEM's 'incremental' named no prior work, and the paper calls itself an extension of existing transforms, so no novelty verdict rests on wrong prior work.
B's spotlight rests on no rating above 7 and a meta-review that names no strength or argument for that tier.
No reviewer read the paper from a neighbouring field's premises.
No reviewer in either committee rated well above the accept level; B's top score is 7.
No one rejected the paper because promised revisions were too large.
Both ACs relied only on the visible record.
Both committees judged the paper as a method paper by the same standard.
rPEM's 5 rested on writing, significance and incrementality, which are central to the contribution, not peripheral points.

reasoning: The panels nearly agree (A 6/7/5/6, B 7/6/7) and named the same weaknesses; the split comes from the area chairs moving in opposite directions. A's AC adopted the lone detractor's late, unanswered list and rejected against three positive scores (R01, R10, R17, R06, R05). B's AC gave a spotlight on unanimity alone with no rating above 7 and no weakness or strength named (R12, R14, R31), after a rebuttal that closed B's concrete gaps but could not fix A's writing and novelty concerns (R03, R20). The two rebuttals also labelled one table row differently (R29). Existing reasons cover every mechanism here, so none was added.
